“(c) 
For the purpose of this section and sect ion 4358 of this title, the portion of a publication devoted to advertisements shall include all advertisements inserted in the publication and attached permanently thereto.


“(d) 

(1) 
Publications mailed in accordance with subsection (a), upon request by the publisher or news agent, may be transported by air on a space-available basis, on scheduled United States air carriers at rates fixed and determined by the Civil Aeronautics Board in accordance with section 406 of the Federal Aviation Act of 1958 (49 U.S.C. 1376). The Postmaster General may authorize the transportation of publications by air pursuant to this subsection only when such transportation does not impede the transportation of airmail, air parcel post, or air transportation of first-class mail on a space-available basis.


“(2) 
The Postmaster General shall prescribe from time to time charges to be collected for matter transported by air pursuant to this section. The charges—

“(A) 
shall be in addition to the payment of lawfully required postage;


“(B) 
may not be adjusted more frequently than once every two years; and


“(C) 
when prescribed or adjusted, shall equal, as nearly as practicable, the amount by which the allocated cost incurred by the Department for the delivery of such matter by air is in excess of the allocated cost which would have been incurred by the Department had such matter been delivered by surface transportation, but the total of such charges and the lawfully required postage shall not, be less than 4 cents per piece.




“(e) 
As used in this section the term ‘zones’ means the eight zones described in section 4553, or prescribed pursuant to section 4558, of this title.”; and

fable.w: The section fixes postage rates by statute and lets the Postmaster General prescribe air-transport charges under a cost formula, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or consultation with any outside party. The tempting reading treats "prescribe charges" as rulemaking, or the publisher's "request" for air transport as participation. But the text does not call for regulations or any public process, and the publisher's request is simply a request for a service, akin to an application. The Civil Aeronautics Board reference is to another federal agency setting rates under a different statute.
fable.s: The Postmaster General shall prescribe from time to time charges to be collected for matter transported by air pursuant to this section.

qwen_block.w: This section details the amendment of postage rates and procedures for air transport of mail. The decisions are made by federal officials (the Postmaster General) and federal agencies (the Civil Aeronautics Board). There is no requirement for consultation with or participation by non-federal entities such as the public, states, or private organizations in the decision-making process. The mention of a publisher's request is for a service, not for influencing a policy decision through participation.
qwen_block.s: The Postmaster General shall prescribe from time to time charges to be collected for matter transported by air pursuant to this section.
qwen_block.b:
Temptation: The text mentions the "Civil Aeronautics Board" and "Postmaster General" making decisions, which might suggest some form of consultation or advisory process. However, the Civil Aeronautics Board is a federal agency (inside the government), and the Postmaster General is a federal official. The text primarily lists postage rates and administrative procedures for mail transport. There is no mention of public comment periods, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states, tribes, or the general public.

Resolution: This section amends statutes regarding postage rates and mail transportation procedures. It involves federal officials (Postmaster General) and federal agencies (Civil Aeronautics Board) setting rates and rules. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with people outside the government (such as the public, states, or private entities) before making these decisions. The "request by the publisher" in subsection (d)(1) is a service request for air transport, not participation in a policy decision. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.

opus.w: This section sets postage rates, defines terms and makes small wording changes. It does not require or allow consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies or lawsuits by anyone outside the federal government. Reading the Postmaster General's power to 'prescribe' charges as rulemaking is tempting, but unlike Example 6 it never says 'by regulation.' The charges come from a set cost formula and are a federal official's own decision. The Civil Aeronautics Board reference only uses rates already fixed under another statute and creates no new outside-party process.
opus.s: The Postmaster General shall prescribe from time to time charges to be collected for matter transported by air pursuant to this section.
opus.b: **Tempting reading:** "The Postmaster General shall prescribe from time to time charges" looks like rulemaking, and the reference to Civil Aeronautics Board rate-setting under section 406 points to a process that elsewhere involves hearings with carriers. Both readings are weak. The section never says the charges must be set "by regulation," which is what made Example 6 a "Yes." The section 406 reference only borrows rates the Board has already set; it does not require any new hearing, comment period or consultation with outside parties here. Everything else is a rate table, definitions and wording changes. I'm only moderately confident, because "prescribe charges" could arguably count as rulemaking authority.

qwen_chat.w: The section establishes postage rates and procedures for air transport of publications. While it mentions the Civil Aeronautics Board, that entity is a federal agency, so its role is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for public comment, hearings, or consultation with non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: Publications mailed in accordance with subsection (a), upon request by the publisher or news agent, may be transported by air on a space-available basis, on scheduled United States air carriers at rates fixed and determined by the Civil Aeronautics Board in accordance with section 406 of the Federal Aviation Act of 1958 (49 U.S.C. 1376).
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions the "Civil Aeronautics Board" fixing rates.
Resolution: The Civil Aeronautics Board is a federal agency (or was at the time), so its involvement is intra-governmental. The section primarily sets postage rates and procedures for the Postmaster General, with no requirement for public comment, hearings, or consultation with outside entities.
